excerpt: Stripe Treasury combines your payments and finances so you can store, spend, and send money from a single place.
A financial account can hold fiat balances such as USD, EUR, and GBP, and eligible businesses can also hold a stablecoin balance in USDC.
There are no monthly fees or minimum balance requirements to open or maintain a financial account.
you can access your financial account on the Treasury page in the Stripe Dashboard or from the Dashboard mobile app
allows Connect platforms to offer financial services, such as funds separation and storage, bill pay, and cash flow management, to eligible connected accounts
Allow businesses to store funds, add recipients, and pay contractors and vendors.
Create financial accounts that can hold funds (`money_manager` configuration)
Render Stripe financial account features such as bill pay, issuing, and cash rewards as a branded UI in your platform application while avoiding custom coding and compliance reviews.
As the platform, you can move money from your payments [Balance] to your financial accounts or from your connected accounts’ payments balance to their financial accounts.
OutboundPayment objects represent push-based transfers from: A platform’s financial accounts to a financial account owned by connected accounts.
You can authorize third parties to debit funds from a financial account.
You can embed the Treasury disclosure component directly on your website to automatically display currently compliant disclosure information without requiring future code changes.
Use transactions to build account activity feeds, reconcile against your internal systems, and track money movement through your platform.
Stripe runs automatic risk controls that help reduce your fraud exposure within Treasury and Issuing without requiring action to enable.
You can use Treasury for platforms to enable your connected accounts to hold funds, pay bills, and manage their cash flow.
Stripe Treasury for Platforms provides users with a container for money called a FinancialAccount that is separate from their Payments balance.
Send funds from a Stripe payments balance | Instant | Stripe API
You can authorize third parties to debit funds from a financial account. Any transaction initiated after this authorization generates a ReceivedDebit object
Every movement of funds into or out of a financial account creates a Transaction object. Transactions are the ledger entries for your financial accounts.
v2.money_management.transaction.created | A flow creates a transaction on a financial account.
Launch Stripe Treasury and Issuing for platforms as a prebuilt set of embeddable components... while avoiding custom coding and compliance reviews.

Platform-owned Treasury controls: Build and operate controls for account onboarding, bank account linking, inbound transfers, outbound money movement, received credits, returns, negative balances, and financial account feature changes.

If anyone is searching for an offering that's a bit more mature and not invite only, I highly recommend Synapse as a Banking as a Service platform.
This would have saved years of development effort and maintenance on treasury operations for my team at a previous gig (live events/ticketing space).

Stripe starts with an API service and later introduces their own product competing with early adopters — a good example is Stripe Billing. I wouldn't be surprised to see Stripe launching their own virtual bank product.
It all seems very Stripe-locked-in and would only work with payments going via Stripe... marketplaces that support PayPal are out?

If I were to build a Bank on top of this, what's stopping Stripe from coming up with their own Banking service that undercuts my bank on every financial metric? Stripe Corporate Card came out almost immediately after Stripe Issuing.

Stripe PM (tarstarr) described use cases: bank account replacement for SMBs (e.g., Shopify building Balance with the Treasury API so merchants can manage revenue and spend in one place), open loop wallets, and platform-level reserve/chargeback balances.
Escrow has a precise legal definition—while we don't support straight-up 'escrow,' Stripe recently added support to hold funds for up to 3 months via Connect's manual payouts.
Stripe employee (patio11): 'We don't support using Payments to collect loan repayments in most cases,' regarding whether Treasury accounts could be used for drivers repaying vehicle loans/leases.
Question raised: 'Just curious, who gets paid the interest on these accounts?' regarding Treasury's interest-earning feature for platform-held balances.
